text:
Alex Martinez: trying to unblock docs + SDK snippet updates for tiered batching. main open question: where does this live on docs site? API ref? Optimize guides? both?

Monica Patel: +1. also need stable terminology before I touch python/ts/go examples. right now I’ve seen `cost_efficient`, “cost-efficient”, and “eco” in different places :grimacing:

Elliot Price: current docs IA options:
1) `Guides -> Performance -> Batching` (new page) + short callout in each endpoint page
2) `Optimize -> Recommendations -> Batching profiles` (since PM wants it tied to Optimize messaging)
3) both, but we need a single canonical definition + link hygiene

Wei Chen: if we bury this under Optimize only, Hosted API users won’t find it. they mostly live in `/docs/api` and copy/paste snippets from endpoint docs.

Soojin Lee: from product messaging side we should keep “batching tiers” consistent with SLO language: Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient.
- customer-facing names: “Fast”, “Standard”, “Cost-efficient”
- config values: TBD but ideally predictable
Also pls avoid “eco” externally (feels cute and ambiguous).

Alex Martinez: ok, so proposal:
- new guide page under Guides/Performance (primary)
- endpoint docs get a short “Batching tier” section with snippet + link to guide
- Optimize page can reference it but not be the only home

Monica Patel: works. but I need exact naming for the SDK param. do we want `batching_tier` w/ values `fast|standard|cost_efficient`?

Nikhil Sharma: on the API side we already have an internal param draft as `batching_tier`. values in runtime config are `fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient`.
I’m good exposing those; they’re boring but stable.

Lena Fischer: fwiw runtime schema PR uses `cost_efficient` (underscore) b/c YAML/JSON friendly + matches existing config conventions. docs can render it as “Cost-efficient” in prose.

Wei Chen: can we please include an example that shows precedence with explicit knobs? support keeps getting “I set tier but queue_delay didn’t change” type confusion.

Alex Martinez: yep, should add an “Overrides and precedence” section:
- explicit knobs win over tier
- tier fills defaults only
- “effective config” can be inspected via Console / explain endpoint (once live)

Monica Patel: for SDK snippets, I can do something like:

```python
client.responses.create(
  model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  input="…",
  extra={
    "batching_tier": "standard"
  }
)
```

But if we want a nicer surface, we’ll need typing changes. we promised no breaking API changes. so probably keep it in existing per-request config bag.

Nikhil Sharma: yep, no new top-level field in request schema for beta. keep it inside the existing `runtime_config` / `extra` object. we can revisit ergonomic wrapper post-beta.

Elliot Price: doc clarity ask: we should state *where* the tier applies.
- per route (chat/completions/embeddings)
- per deployment (Dedicated/Private default)
- can be set at account/model policy level (later)

Soojin Lee: and we need a one-liner per tier that’s not hand-wavy.
Fast: lowest queueing, best streaming cadence, higher $/token.
Standard: balanced default.
Cost-efficient: higher batching/queueing, best $/token, may increase p95/p99.

Wei Chen: + add a “Streaming note” callout. people equate batching with “slower streaming”. we should say Fast prioritizes decode to keep token cadence, cost-efficient trades cadence for throughput.

Alex Martinez: action items:
- Elliot: draft page location + outline (Guides/Performance). also add endpoint doc callout template.
- Wei: update Hosted API endpoint pages with callout once outline lands.
- Monica: prep SDK snippet PRs w/ `batching_tier` inside existing config bag; include both minimal example + override example.
- Soojin: confirm final customer-facing names (Fast/Standard/Cost-efficient) and approve copy.

Monica Patel: can we get one canonical snippet we can reuse across python/ts/go? like a “golden” snippet that shows tier + one override.

Alex Martinez: yes. something like:

```json
{
  "batching_tier": "cost_efficient",
  "batching": {
    "max_queue_delay_ms": 12
  }
}
```

and in docs we explain `batching.max_queue_delay_ms` overrides the tier default.

Lena Fischer: careful: naming for override field is still `batching_policy` vs `batching` in some configs. pls don’t cement until Ethan confirms. I’ll ping him.

Wei Chen: +1. last thing we want is docs locking in an internal struct name.

Alex Martinez: good catch. Monica hold off on override example until we confirm the exact key name from runtime config schema.

Monica Patel: ok. I’ll do tier-only snippets first; add override snippet after schema lands.

Soojin Lee: also: please don’t mix “SLO tier” and “batching tier” in the same sentence without clarifying. customers will assume it changes their contract. maybe: “Batching tier (performance profile)” and separately “Latency SLO tier”.

Elliot Price: I’ll include a glossary box:
- *Batching tier*: selects recommended runtime batching defaults.
- *Latency SLO tier*: contractual target/alerts.
And note they’re aligned but not equivalent.

Wei Chen: can we add a FAQ entry: “Why did my p95 get worse on cost-efficient?” with a checklist (watch queue delay, timeouts, concurrency). even a short one helps support.

Alex Martinez: yes, FAQ section on the guide page.

Lena Fischer: update from Ethan is pending, but current plan is `runtime_config.batching_tier` + optional `runtime_config.batching_overrides` (name not final). I’ll reply in thread once confirmed.

Monica Patel: :thumbsup: once key names are locked I’ll push PRs:
- redwood-sdk-python: update examples + docstrings
- redwood-sdk-typescript: typing + example
- redwood-examples: one app sets `batching_tier=standard`

Alex Martinez: cool. please link PRs here when ready so we can keep terminology consistent across repos.

Elliot Price: I’ll open a docs tracking issue w/ checkboxes (page, callouts, FAQ, snippets). will drop link once created.
